metadata.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Computer-Assisted Learning and AI-guided Tutors

extraction.outcome_summary: The article reviewed recent evidence on computer-assisted learning and AI-guided tutoring, concluding that well-designed systems can improve learning, especially in mathematics, but that effects depend heavily on implementation quality, teacher support, and pedagogical design. Its Italy-focused empirical analysis used Google Trends data as a proxy for ChatGPT adoption in education and found strong regional and seasonal variation, with adoption initially higher in wealthier regions but converging over time. The PISA-based descriptive evidence showed that digital resource shortages remained more concentrated in disadvantaged and rural schools, underscoring persistent equity concerns despite Italy’s relatively favorable national position. The study was open access and relied on publicly available PISA and Google Trends data rather than student-level achievement modeling.
